source.title: The hippocampal indexing theory and episodic memory: updating the index

confidence_rationale: Established hippocampal theory with extensive empirical grounding. It supports cue-conditioned access to distributed cortical representations, which is adjacent to MECH-547, but supplies a strong rival: hippocampus can coordinate heterogeneous downstream content by indexing and reinstating the appropriate cortical ensemble without computing a latent-to-latent receiver-conditioned translation. Mixed is deliberate: the paper strengthens the need for context-sensitive access while weakening any hippocampus-as-translator interpretation.
failure_signatures: If simple indexed reinstatement of the appropriate stored cortical/latent state reproduces the benefit attributed to T(A,B), MECH-547's translation-specific interpretation is unnecessary.
If receiver-state permutation leaves performance intact while cue/index identity matters, the data favour indexing over receiver-conditioned translation.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The hippocampus stores an index over distributed neocortical activity patterns; partial cues can reactivate the relevant hippocampal index and thereby reinstate the associated cortical representation.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports the general need for context/cue-selective access to distributed representations while supplying a lower-complexity rival to a learned receiver-conditioned bridge: index the correct relational/episodic state and reinstate it.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The indexing theory is not a theory of latent-space coordinate transformation and predates modern population-geometry methods. Treat it as a rival mechanism, not direct disconfirmation of MECH-547.
mapping.source_context: Review/update of hippocampal memory indexing theory and its empirical support.

confidence_components.notes: High conceptual relevance as a rival; no direct artificial-system transfer.
